findings.check: Extra check 1: the rule that fails to see such a path (hasHomePath in tools/src/traces), a finding of tools-core named here, not fixed
findings.title: The traces check and the pre-push gate do not see Windows paths: only /Users/<name>, /home/<name> and the encoded form are looked for, and the temporary-folder rule knows only /tmp roots
findings.where: tools/src/traces/rules.js:7-16 (HOME_PATH, HOME_ENCODED, hasHomePath) and :20-22 (TEMP_ROOT); tools/src/traces/check.js:145; docs/design/REQ-014-traces.md and docs/requirements.yaml REQ-014 (the criterion names 'macOS and Linux' home folders only)
findings.evidence: rules.js:9: const HOME_PATH = /(?:^|[^A-Za-z0-9._-])\/(?:Users|home)\/[A-Za-z0-9._-]/u;  rules.js:12: HOME_ENCODED needs '-Users-<name>-'. A Windows path in a JSON handoff is C:\\Users\\<name>\\... (backslashes, no slash), so neither pattern matches. Command: cd tools && npm run -s traces in the fixed copy of f72eaa7 (26 files with the path) -> 'traces: файлов проверено 2903, следов 0, пропущено 67'; in the current project (8 files) -> 'файлов проверено 2919, следов 0, пропущено 67'. The cause is by design: the requirement text of REQ-014 lists macOS and Linux only (docs/requirements.yaml, REQ-014 criterion, 'пути домашних каталогов пользователей macOS и Linux'). The gap was noted once in handoffs/E2E104-20261103-01/step-01f-code-design-validator.json ('a Windows path with backslashes (C:\Users\...) is not seen by hasHomePath') and never opened as a defect (grep of docs/issues: 0). The owner works on Windows since 2026-10-30.
findings.item: Q7 and REQ-014 (traces of the PC in the repository); the pre-push gate .githooks/pre-push relies on it
findings.recommendation: Open a defect for tools-core: extend the rule for Windows (a drive letter, a backslash or a slash and the folder Users, in plain, JSON-escaped (two backslashes) and slash form, and the Windows temporary-folder forms AppData\Local\Temp and /c/Users/); change the REQ-014 criterion and design text first (the requirement says macOS and Linux only), then the tests in tools/test for traces with a Windows line in plain, escaped and Git-Bash form. ORCH decides about the defect (plan open point 3).

One line (the hash is 64 characters; first 12 shown): "write-secret 465f654a88e7..., 44 bytes, 2026-10-01 22:52:26 (the hash of the file, not the secret)" in handoffs/E2E106-20261115-01/step-01d-code-design-validator.json. findings.item: Q7 (not a secret itself: a 256-bit hash of a 32-byte random file cannot be reversed; it is a fingerprint of the real key in a public repository)
findings.recommendation: No rewrite of history needed. Write the next control without the full digest (compare in the test by the digest held in a scratch file, quote only the first 8 characters, or 'equal / not equal'). If the owner wants, rotate the write secret at the next Pixel Office start, then the old fingerprint is of no use.

findings.recommendation: Owner: switch on 'Secret scanning' and 'Push protection' in the repository settings (free for public repositories). Optional for tools-core: a key-pattern step in the traces check with the patterns of this audit (not a requirement now).

summary.text: No real secret in the 2903 files of handoffs/, runs/ and reports/ (every key-like hit is a test fixture or a name). The problems are private data of the owner's computers: after the clean-up commit 6cb68b1 the Windows user name and the scratch path are back in 8 handoffs of the current project (none on origin yet), the traces check is blind to Windows paths by the wording of REQ-014 and would let them through the pre-push gate, and the login name of the old Mac stays in 7 handoffs on origin/main. A file hash of the real Pixel Office write secret is in 36 public handoffs (Low), and secret scanning is off on the public repository (Low).
